```{r setup}
library(ermeeth2)
```

`ermeeth2` gathers the functions used by the ThreeME team to run, post-process
and document ThreeME v4 simulations. It is the successor to `ermeeth`.

## The long-format data shape

Most of the plotting and table functions work on a long-format dataframe with
the columns:

| column | content |
|---|---|
| `year` | simulation year |
| `variable` | ThreeME variable code |
| `scenario` | scenario name |
| `values` | value of the variable in that scenario |
| `values_ref` | value of the variable in the baseline |
| `index_scen` | 1 for the baseline scenario, 0 otherwise |

`sector` and `commodity` are added when the variable code carries a sector or
commodity suffix.

## Where to start

- `long_data()` / `wide_data()` to reshape simulation output
- `threeme_transform()` for the ways a variable can be looked at: level,
  relative difference, absolute difference, percentage points, growth rate,
  index
- `simple_plot()` to draw a set of variables, over one or several scenarios
- `table_3me()` to build a result table, optionally comparing two versions of
  the model
- `run_simulations()` to run a set of scenarios

## Naming variables in the model: avoid `elem_<...>_<year>`

**Do not give a variable of the model a name of the form
`elem_<name>_<year>`**, such as `elem_gdp_2019`.

The R solver has no `@elem()`. Before solving, each `@elem()` of the model is
replaced by a constant holding its value, and that constant is named after
what it stands for:

| in the `.mdl` | becomes |
|---|---|
| `@elem(GDP, 2019)` | `elem_gdp_2019` |
| `@elem(PK_SIND(-1), 2019)` | `elem_pk_sind_2018` (the lag is folded into the year) |
| `@elem(CHD_CIND/CHM_CIND, 2015)` | `elem_chd_cind_chm_cind_2015` |

A variable of the model that already has one of these names is silently
overwritten by the constant, in the calibration and in every scenario, and no
message says so. Names are compared without regard to case.

These constants are not written to the results (name one in
`variables_to_keep` to keep it). Names that only contain `ELEM`, such as
`TELEM_X` or `ELEMENT_Y`, are not concerned.
